**Build it yourself.** [Read the tutorial](../read/extra-01.qmd) is the other way to read this part.

If you start at this part, make your clone as **Get the project** says, and then run this command. It puts in your clone the files that this part starts from. A file that the project deleted before this part stays, so delete it if `git check` lists it:

```bash
git rm -rq --cached --ignore-unmatch -- :/ && git restore --source 974d653080b0 --staged --worktree -- :/
```

```bash
just setup
```

A list of counts is hard to read at a glance. A table lines up the words and the counts. A small package,
tabulate, draws tables, so tally depends on it. The docs come later, and their tool comes now, in a group of its own.

[The code before this part](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/tree/974d653080b0bd7dd06741b60225518cfecc908e). [The code after it](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/tree/ec6a8aa7f9a8b81ef07c6c8ec69f01307482dc32).

## 1.1 tabulate, in a range of versions {#extra-01.1}

tally needs tabulate to draw a table. A new version 1.0 of tabulate could change how it draws one, so tally takes
any 0.9 version, and no later one. `uv add` with a range of versions puts the range in `pyproject.toml`, and the
exact version in `uv.lock`:

The author ran `uv add "tabulate>=0.9,<0.10"` here. It writes `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. On a later day, it can write newer versions of packages than the author's, and then git check finds that your files differ. So do not run it. Run this command in its place, from the top of the project. It takes each file as the author has it from the project, and installs exactly the versions that `uv.lock` names:

```bash
git restore --source 418e7fd88a3f -- pyproject.toml uv.lock && uv sync --locked --all-groups --all-packages
```

```bash
uv run python -c "import tabulate; print(tabulate.__version__)"
```

It prints `0.9.0`.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check 418e7fd88a3f
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source 974d653080b0 --staged -- :/ && git restore --source 418e7fd88a3f --staged --worktree -- :/
```

### What changed {#extra-01.1-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="extra-01.1-pyproject.toml-5d07e7"></a>`pyproject.toml`: tabulate, with the range of its versions. 3 lines added, 1 removed. It comes from `uv add "tabulate>=0.9,<0.10"`, and you take it from the project. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/418e7fd88a3f64b2a5a0f2ebd14b301694ce821e/pyproject.toml).
  - look at `"tabulate>=0.9,<0.10",`
- <a id="extra-01.1-uv.lock-8356d8"></a>`uv.lock`: the exact version of tabulate. 13 lines added. It comes from `uv add "tabulate>=0.9,<0.10"`, and you take it from the project. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/418e7fd88a3f64b2a5a0f2ebd14b301694ce821e/uv.lock).

<details><summary>The diff that <code>uv add "tabulate&gt;=0.9,&lt;0.10"</code> makes in <code>pyproject.toml</code>, which you take from the project</summary>

## 1.2 tally --table {#extra-01.2}

tally prints one line for each word, with the count first. A new option, `--table`, prints the same counts as a
table, with a header. `main` takes the option out of the arguments, and passes the rows to `tabulate`.

Apply the patch to [`src/tally/__init__.py`](#extra-01.2-src-tally-__init__.py-b5485b), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/5051c3ff6e71020d5458c29a2e4a1f358d361b16.diff | git apply --include=src/tally/__init__.py
```

The patch adds `from tabulate import tabulate` under `import sys`, after a blank line. In `main`, it adds the flag
`as_table`, and prints the rows with `tabulate` when the flag is set.

```bash
uv run tally --top 3 --table data/corpus.txt
```

It prints a header, `word` and `times`, a line of dashes, and the three words with their counts in a column on the
right.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check 5051c3ff6e71
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source 418e7fd88a3f --staged -- :/ && git restore --source 5051c3ff6e71 --staged --worktree -- :/
```

### What changed {#extra-01.2-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="extra-01.2-src-tally-__init__.py-b5485b"></a>`src/tally/__init__.py`: the option `--table`, which prints the rows with tabulate. 11 lines added, 3 removed. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/5051c3ff6e71020d5458c29a2e4a1f358d361b16/src/tally/__init__.py).
  - look at `print(tabulate(rows, headers=["word", "times"]))`

<details open><summary>The patch to <code>src/tally/__init__.py</code></summary>

```diff
@@ -2,6 +2,8 @@
 
 import sys
 
+from tabulate import tabulate
+
 
 def count(text: str) -> dict[str, int]:
     "How many times each word of `text` appears, ignoring case."
@@ -17,11 +19,17 @@ def top(counts: dict[str, int], n: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
 
 
 def main() -> None:
-    "Count the words of a file, or of the standard input. With --top N, only the N most common."
-    args, n = sys.argv[1:], None
+    "Count the words of a file, or of the standard input. Options: --top N, and --table."
+    args = sys.argv[1:]
+    as_table = "--table" in args
+    args, n = [arg for arg in args if arg != "--table"], None
     if args[:1] == ["--top"]:
         n, args = int(args[1]), args[2:]
     text = open(args[0]).read() if args else sys.stdin.read()
     counts = count(text)
-    for word, times in top(counts, n) if n else sorted(counts.items()):
+    rows = top(counts, n) if n else sorted(counts.items())
+    if as_table:
+        print(tabulate(rows, headers=["word", "times"]))
+        return
+    for word, times in rows:
         print(times, word)
```

</details>

[This change on GitHub](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/5051c3ff6e71020d5458c29a2e4a1f358d361b16). [The code after it](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/tree/5051c3ff6e71020d5458c29a2e4a1f358d361b16).

## 1.3 mdformat, in the group docs {#extra-01.3}

The docs will be Markdown files. mdformat formats Markdown, and its option `--check` says whether a file is
formatted. Only the people who write the docs need it, so it goes in a group of its own, `docs`:

The author ran `uv add --group docs mdformat` here. It writes `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. On a later day, it can write newer versions of packages than the author's, and then git check finds that your files differ. So do not run it. Run this command in its place, from the top of the project. It takes each file as the author has it from the project, and installs exactly the versions that `uv.lock` names:

```bash
git restore --source ec6a8aa7f9a8 -- pyproject.toml uv.lock && uv sync --locked --all-groups --all-packages
```

`uv sync` installs the group `dev` and no other group, unless the project names more. One more line in the table
`[tool.uv]` of `pyproject.toml` names both groups, so that `just setup` installs mdformat too.

The command above took [`pyproject.toml`](#extra-01.3-pyproject.toml-5d07e7) from the project with this change in it already, so there is nothing to apply.

After `uv add`, the patch adds a table `[tool.uv]` at the end of `pyproject.toml`, with the line `default-groups`.

```bash
uv sync -q && uv run --no-sync mdformat --version
```

`uv sync` installs mdformat. Then `uv run --no-sync` runs it without another sync, and it prints `mdformat 1.0.0`, or a
newer version.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check ec6a8aa7f9a8
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source 5051c3ff6e71 --staged -- :/ && git restore --source ec6a8aa7f9a8 --staged --worktree -- :/
```

### What changed {#extra-01.3-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="extra-01.3-pyproject.toml-5d07e7"></a>`pyproject.toml`: the group `docs`, and the groups that `uv sync` installs. 6 lines added. It comes from `uv add --group docs mdformat`, and you take it from the project. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/ec6a8aa7f9a8b81ef07c6c8ec69f01307482dc32/pyproject.toml).
  - look at `default-groups = ["dev", "docs"]`
- <a id="extra-01.3-uv.lock-8356d8"></a>`uv.lock`: the exact versions of mdformat and of the packages it needs. 37 lines added. It comes from `uv add --group docs mdformat`, and you take it from the project. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/ec6a8aa7f9a8b81ef07c6c8ec69f01307482dc32/uv.lock).

<details><summary>The diff that <code>uv add --group docs mdformat</code> makes in <code>pyproject.toml</code>, which you take from the project</summary>

```diff
@@ -19,6 +19,12 @@ build-backend = "uv_build"
 dev = [
     "ruff>=0.17.0",
 ]
+docs = [
+    "mdformat>=1.0.0",
+]
 
 [tool.ruff]
 line-length = 100
+
+[tool.uv]
+default-groups = ["dev", "docs"]
```

</details>
